title: The Storm That Changed How I See the Sea
script: Narrator: [calm] Last month, I rented a small wooden house near the coast, because I wanted a quiet week away from my noisy apartment in the city.
Narrator: [thoughtful] On the third evening, the sky turned a strange greenish color, and the fishermen on the beach started pulling their boats up quickly.
Narrator: [nervous] I asked one of them what was happening, and he simply said, a storm is coming, go inside now and stay away from the windows.
Narrator: [with feeling] Within an hour, the wind grew so strong that the whole house creaked, and the waves crashed against the rocks like something alive and angry.
Narrator: [honestly] I was frightened, although I was safe inside, because I had never seen the sea behave with such raw, uncontrollable power before.
Narrator: [reflective] I sat by the small window and watched for almost two hours, unable to look away even though my hands were shaking slightly.
Narrator: [gently] Around midnight, the wind finally calmed, and the rain softened into a gentle patter on the roof above my head.
Narrator: [warmly] The next morning, I walked out to a completely different beach. The sand was smoother, and strange shells had washed up everywhere along the shore.
Narrator: [thoughtful] The same fisherman was already back near his boat, checking the ropes calmly, as if nothing unusual had happened the night before.
Narrator: [curious] I asked him if storms like that scared him after so many years of fishing this coast.
Narrator: [reflective] He smiled and said the sea gives generously most days, so he doesn't complain when it occasionally reminds everyone who is truly in control.
Narrator: [with feeling] His answer stayed with me long after I left that coast and returned to my ordinary city routine.
Narrator: [peacefully] Now, whenever I feel like I control everything in my life, I remember that greenish sky and those crashing waves.
Narrator: [warmly] Nature does not need our permission to be powerful, and honestly, that thought makes me feel smaller in a good, humbling way.

options: For a quiet week away from her noisy apartment
quiz.explanation: She rented the house because she wanted a quiet week away from her noisy city apartment.

options: Smoother sand with strange shells washed up everywhere

quiz.question: What did the fisherman say about the sea?
options: It gives generously most days, but sometimes reminds people who is in control
quiz.explanation: He said the sea gives generously most days, so he doesn't complain when it reminds everyone who is truly in control.

quiz.question: What does the narrator think about now, back in her city routine?
options: How to avoid the coast forever
The greenish sky and crashing waves, which remind her she doesn't control everything
quiz.explanation: She now remembers the storm whenever she feels like she controls everything, which humbles her.
